decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with the right arm; raise and turn toward the blue nut, keeping the left arm parked. Final nut alignment will use new views.
Move above the blue nut in the right workspace, finishing a vertical grasp orientation with small continuous increments.
Descend onto the blue nut with a small image-based centering correction, then close the right gripper. Retention is not yet verified.
Lift the blue nut and carry it above the matching blue bolt within the right workspace; keep the gripper closed and the tool upright.
The blue nut is retained. Lower it toward the blue bolt with a small wrist-image centering correction, pausing to inspect engagement before tightening.
Apply a short clockwise tightening stroke to the blue nut with slight axial descent, keeping the right gripper closed and checking that the nut remains upright.
Release the blue nut and reset wrist rotation without axial motion. Inspect whether the nut remains seated on its matching bolt before another tightening stroke.
The blue nut is visibly separate from the bolt after release. Lift the open right hand to clear the view and plan a corrected pickup rather than assuming engagement.
Recenter above the displaced blue nut using both head and wrist views, descending only to a pregrasp height while staying clear of the blue bolt.
Blue nut is centered in the wrist view. Descend vertically to its side-grasp height and close fully; verify retention before transporting.
Allow the right gripper to finish closing, then use a small descent from the observed pose to engage the blue nut sides; the preceding descent had a larger tracking residual.
The adjacent blue bolt appears to obstruct the gripper. Lift open and turn the grasp direction by a quarter turn to approach the nut without straddling the bolt.
Approach the blue nut with the revised jaw direction, correcting the small tool tilt; close fully at the table-level nut grasp height.
Lift the centered blue nut and translate above the blue bolt with a vertical tool, keeping the gripper fully closed. Inspect the axial alignment before lowering.
Lower the retained blue nut toward the bolt tip with a millimeter-scale lateral correction, pausing at the expected thread entry height to inspect centering.
The blue bolt tip is now centered in the retained nut. Apply a controlled clockwise quarter-turn with slight axial feed while maintaining upright alignment.
Release and unwind the right wrist while keeping the blue nut on its bolt, then regrasp for the next tightening stroke. Check seating in the returned views.
The blue nut stayed aligned during release. Tighten another one-third turn with small downward feed, keeping the gripper closed and the tool upright.
Open and reset the right wrist, then regrasp the seated blue nut for another tightening stroke without lifting it.
Continue clockwise tightening of the seated blue nut. In parallel, raise the empty left arm into a continuous elbow-up approach posture for the remaining left-side pairs.
Reset and regrasp the blue nut. Move the empty left hand to a high, vertical standby pose in its own workspace, leaving the center clear for later transfers.
Tighten the aligned blue nut another clockwise third-turn with a small downward thread feed; keep the left hand stationary and clear.
Release and unwind the right wrist while leaving the blue nut seated, then close again for the next clockwise tightening stroke.
Continue tightening the upright blue nut clockwise with a small axial feed, checking the visible screw depth rather than treating tracking as success.
Reset the open right wrist and regrasp the blue nut at its current thread depth. Keep both elbows in their existing raised configuration.
Apply another controlled clockwise tightening stroke to the blue pair with a small thread feed, maintaining the closed grasp and upright axis.
Release the tightened blue nut, lift clear while resetting the wrist, then move above the red nut. The next view will check the blue pair remains together.
Blue pair remains together after release. Descend onto the red nut with a small centering correction and close the right gripper for transfer to the middle.
Recenter the red nut between the fingertips using its wrist-view offset, close again, and lift slightly to verify retention before the middle transfer.
The red nut is retained and better centered. Lift above the bolts and carry it to the middle for a table-mediated transfer, leaving the left hand stationary and clear.
Lower the red nut upright onto the middle of the table and release it for the left arm. Keep the left hand stationary until the right hand clears the transfer area.
Clear the right hand upward, then withdraw it above the gray nut while the left hand approaches the middle red nut. Keep the hands separated and stop at pregrasp heights.
Lower the left hand toward the middle red nut and the right hand toward the gray nut, with small head-view centering corrections. Pause above grasp height to inspect both.
Both nuts are centered in the wrist views. Descend to the side-grasp heights and close both grippers; retention will be checked during a short lift.
Lift both grasped nuts clear. Carry red above its left-side bolt while bringing gray to the middle for transfer; retain both with closed grippers and keep the hands separated.
Lower red toward its bolt with a small wrist-image lateral correction. Place gray upright in the middle and release the right gripper; inspect red thread entry before turning.
Refine red nut centering from the visible bolt tip before tightening. Lift and withdraw the open right hand, leaving gray on the middle of the table for later pickup.
Make a final small lateral correction to the red nut and apply a short clockwise engagement stroke with gentle axial feed. Keep the right arm clear.
The red bolt tip still appears laterally offset in the nut opening. Shift the retained nut a few millimeters at fixed orientation before further tightening.
The red tip is now centered in the opening. Turn clockwise a short stroke, then release in place to check whether the nut stays seated on the bolt.
Reset the open left wrist while leaving the red pair undisturbed. Inspect the nut's shifted seating position before choosing the next grasp height.
The red nut is visibly tilted rather than fastened upright. Raise the open left hand to avoid disturbing it and inspect a recovery grasp.
Prepare an angled recovery approach to the tilted red nut, backing the left wrist away while aligning with its visible face. Remain above contact height and preserve elbow-up continuity.
Lower the angled left hand toward the tilted red nut in small increments, stopping short of the estimated grasp center to inspect clearance and centering.
Center the angled left gripper on the red nut's visible face using small wrist-view corrections, then close for recovery. Do not yet assume the nut is retained.
Lift the recovered red grasp straight up while keeping the jaws closed. Inspect whether the nut separates from the bolt and remains retained before reorienting.
The red nut did not lift with the hand and now appears seated against the bolt. Clear it without further disturbance and return the left hand to a high vertical approach toward the middle gray nut.
Approach the middle gray nut with the left hand, stopping above grasp height. Begin returning the empty right arm toward its origin along a gradual elbow-up path.
Center and grasp the gray nut with the left hand, using the wrist view for a small correction. Finish the empty right arm's gradual return to origin.
Lift the gray nut clear and carry it above the matching left-side bolt with the grasp closed. Settle the empty right arm at origin and inspect gray alignment before descent.
Lower the retained gray nut toward its bolt with a modest lateral correction, stopping near thread-entry height to inspect the tip through the opening before turning.
Bring the gray nut down a few millimeters and recenter the visible bolt tip with a small lateral correction, keeping the gripper closed and avoiding rotation until entry is clearer.
Make a small single-axis correction to center the gray bolt tip inside the retained nut. Hold height and orientation fixed so the next wrist view can verify the correction.
The gray tip is nearly centered. Apply a final millimeter correction and a controlled clockwise quarter-turn with slight axial feed, keeping the nut upright and the grasp closed.
Release the gray nut in place, reset the left wrist, and regrasp. Check that the nut remains seated upright before continuing clockwise tightening.
The gray nut remained seated during the reset. Tighten it clockwise by one-third turn with a small axial feed, keeping the left grasp closed and right arm parked.
Open the left gripper and reset its wrist rotation without lifting the gray nut, then regrasp for further clockwise tightening.
Continue tightening the upright gray nut clockwise with a small axial feed. Keep the left gripper closed and the right hand parked.
Release and reset the left wrist, then close again on the gray nut at its current depth. Keep the nut seated and the right hand at rest.
Tighten the aligned gray nut another clockwise third-turn with a small downward thread feed, maintaining the closed grasp and upright axis.
Reset the open left wrist and regrasp the gray nut without changing its seated height. Continue checking alignment from the wrist view.
Continue clockwise tightening of the seated gray nut with a small axial feed, maintaining upright alignment and keeping the right hand parked.
Reset the open left wrist and regrasp the gray nut at its current depth for the next tightening stroke, leaving the pair seated.
Apply another clockwise tightening stroke to the gray nut with a small axial feed, keeping the grasp closed and its axis upright.
Release the gray nut and lift the open left hand clear while resetting its wrist. Inspect all three pairs without disturbing their seated positions.
The pairs remain together after release. Begin returning the open left hand toward origin on a raised, continuous elbow-up path while keeping the right hand parked.
Finish the left arm's continuous return to origin, make a small right-origin correction, and hold both grippers open while the assembled pairs settle.
Hold both arms at origin with open grippers and let all three matched pairs settle. Their seated appearance is not by itself proof of completion.

Completion remains uncertain, especially for the recovered red nut. Raise the open left arm along the established elbow-up approach to inspect and, if needed, finish that pair; leave blue and gray undisturbed.
Move the open left hand above the red pair and restore a vertical approach orientation. Inspect the red nut before attempting any further tightening.
Approach the now-upright red nut with an open left gripper and a small centering correction. Stop above contact to check its current seating depth.
The red nut appears upright and deeply seated. Lower to its present side-grasp height and close without lifting or translating it.
Turn the upright red nut clockwise while using minimal axial feed because it already appears deeply seated. Keep the grasp closed and avoid lifting the pair.
Reset the open left wrist without moving the red pair, then regrasp its upright nut for another careful tightening stroke.
Tighten the upright red nut clockwise with minimal axial feed because its bolt tip is already nearly flush. Keep the other pairs undisturbed.
Release the deeply seated red nut and lift clear. Raise the empty right arm along its elbow-up approach so the remaining blue and gray thread depths can be inspected and finished if needed.
